chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: European audiences who know your solos
summary: Danes and Swedes studied recordings; he mentions the Netherlands and Ben Webster in Amsterdam.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You probably found people very, very familiar with all your recordings and everything? in those countries.
Oh, yes, they really study. They know everything you're going -- they know all of your solos. They'll hum along or remind you of this solo that you played in such and such a piece and were very nice.
And was this true of one country any more than the people of other countries, that one country was most concerned with detail and history and listening carefully?

Well, I would say Denmark is good at that, of course, Sweden. Norway is a little -- well, it gets cold up there, I guess, so it's a little less westernized or not as promoted as Sweden and Denmark. The Netherlands, I've only been there once, and that was around in '30's, and they still had their colloquial type of living, you know, the streets, long streets with all the houses look alike. I wonder what they do when somebody gets drunk, how they ever get home.
How do you suppose Ben Webster managed (unintelligible)? He lived in Amsterdam.
Ben? Oh, Ben is -- yeah, well, Ben doesn't drink.
So, you know, it was a wonderful experience.
